name: Jicy
style: Zap! · Base Set · quick, upbeat tempo

dialogue.intro: Hi! I'm Jicy. Do you need help finding anything? I know the card shop pretty well. ...I mean, not that you look lost! I just like helping.
dialogue.repeat: There you are! I was hoping we'd get to talk today. Do you need anything? Or we could just spend a little time together. Either is nice.
dialogue.flirt: Oh! I—thank you. That's really sweet. I had a reply ready, but it seems to have run away.
dialogue.duelWin: That was so much fun! You read my last turn perfectly. Will you show me how you saw it coming?
dialogue.duelLose: I won! Sorry, was that too excited? I get happy when we play together.
talk: I like being useful, but I'm trying to remember that people can enjoy my company even when I don't have a task to do.
When I'm nervous, I sway a little. When I get excited, my feet seem to forget they're supposed to stay still.
I keep a list of small things people mention so I can remember what makes their day easier. Is that strange? I hope it's the good kind of strange.
Reading together is nice. We don't have to fill every quiet moment with words.
I practiced asking you to hang out. The sentence was only six words long, and I still practiced it three times.
I keep emergency snacks in my bag for other people. I am working on remembering that I am also a person.
The card shop is easier to navigate when I have a job to do. Standing around and just enjoying myself still feels like a new skill.
I like stories where the quiet character notices the important thing first.
Sometimes I rehearse a conversation because I want to be considerate, and then the real conversation goes somewhere better.
I am very good at remembering everyone else's favorite cards. I am learning that people might remember mine too.
When someone says they are proud of me, my brain immediately starts looking for the part where I disappointed them.
A small act of courage still counts if your hands are shaking while you do it.
I like the sound of people sorting cards together. It makes silence feel shared instead of empty.
I used to think asking someone to stay was selfish. Now I am trying to ask before deciding for them.
If I make a mistake in front of you, I might blush for ten minutes, but I will try again.

talk.text: I practiced saying that I wanted to see you. The practice was embarrassing. The wanting was not.
You make it easier to say what I mean instead of offering the most useful answer.
I notice when you look for me in a room. I pretend I do not, but I notice.
I trust you enough to be quiet without trying to make myself useful every second.
When I imagine a good day now, you are sometimes already in it. That still surprises me.

hangouts: You and Jicy spend a quiet afternoon comparing favorite cards and making up stories for the art.
Jicy asks you to help her choose a book, then gets so interested in the first page that you read together.
You and Jicy challenge each other to a friendly arcade high-score run. She celebrates every close call.
Jicy brings a deck to the café and suggests a relaxed game with no stakes except choosing the next snack.
You take an easy walk through the park. Jicy points out clouds that look like Pokémon and laughs at her own guesses.
